gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa draws round bowls at a single weight, while Fanwood Text keeps its stems a touch heavier than its hairlines. Over a full page, that plain sans moves along without tiring the eye.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga lays flat, single-weight letters out with generous tracking, so every word looks opened up. And Fanwood Text, a serif, carries the restrained swell of a round brush barely pressed.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, every stem and tail alike. Against Fanwood Text, whose curves lighten mildly toward their ends, that rope-like consistency is the pair's whole character.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-peta: Fanwood Text curves with the slight thickening of a reed pen, editorial and classic. Lexend Peta counters with spaghetti-like, same-width strokes and a big x-height, and that difference is the pair's real draw.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-tera: Fanwood Text is a serif with subtle modulation, editorial and quietly classic. Lexend Tera, a sans with neon-tube strokes and letters spaced like stepping stones, would carry a page at a steady, open pace.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-lexend-zetta: Widely tracked and ribbon-flat, Lexend Zetta moves slowly across a line. Next to Fanwood Text, a serif with mild letterpress-slug variation, that flat sans-serif line stands out, and the gap is what makes the pair.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-gf-montserrat-altern: Contemporary and monoline, Montserrat Alternates crowds its chalk-board lowercase up toward the capital line. And across a full paragraph, that plain sans keeps a brisk, uniform texture beside Fanwood Text.
gen-gf-farsan-author: Farsan has no hairlines anywhere, only strokes like bent pipe cleaner. Author's serif bowls swell gently, so a few lines of text move at a dignified, unhurried pace without any of the heading's bluntness.
gen-gf-farsan-gf-hepta-slab: Farsan sets bold, tightly spaced letters with no hairlines anywhere. Hepta Slab, a serif with stretched-out words and open counters, gives that punch somewhere gentler to rest on the page.
gen-gf-farsan-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Without a single hairline, Farsan packs bold letters tightly together. But Padyakke Expanded One, a serif with spread-out glyphs and unswelling bowls, loosens everything, and that tension is what makes the pair.
